subject: Sync request — throughput & latency sizing for CloudWave search
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <echen@cloudwave.io>, Jake Torres <jake.torres@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Sync request — throughput & latency sizing for CloudWave search

Hi Emily / Jake,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — really helpful to understand how CloudWave plans to use retrieval-augmented generation inside your worker search product. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Goal: move from prototype to a dedicated inference pool for production search augmentation (multi-tenant routing inside CloudWave, strict p95 latency targets).
- Primary constraints you called out: ~200 concurrent search requests during peak (burst to 500), median request size ~120 tokens, target p95 latency < 180ms, and strict data residency in us-west-2.
- Success criteria for the pilot: 95% of searches under 200ms p95, cost target <$0.003/token for inference, and no dropped requests during 5-min spikes.

We recommend a dedicated sizing call (technical deep dive) so Marcus (our Senior SRE for Dedicated) can collect the concrete workload traces and walk through batching, KV cache behavior, and fallback policies. That session usually takes 45 minutes and we come prepared with an initial capacity sketch and a list of concrete inputs we’ll need. 

Proposed times (all PT):
- Tue 24 Feb — 10:00–10:45
- Wed 25 Feb — 14:00–14:45
- Thu 26 Feb — 09:30–10:15

If none of these work, send a couple of windows that do. I’ve attached a short intake template (redwood-intake-template.pdf) and a small example CSV where you can paste representative request counts and token distributions (cloudwave-initial-metrics.csv) — filling that out before the call will let us provide a tighter sketch.

Also: please confirm if the pilot will be hosted in your us-west-2 VPC (good for Private mode) or if you want us to propose a Hosted + Dedicated hybrid as an interim.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a time.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: cloudwave-initial-metrics.csv (CSV, 6 KB)

From: Emily Chen <echen@cloudwave.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jake Torres <jake.torres@cloudwave.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sync request — throughput & latency sizing for CloudWave search

Hi Aditya,

Appreciate the clear recap. Tue/Wed/Thu windows mostly work — Wed 25 Feb 14:00–14:45 PT is the best for our team. Marcus, can you confirm you’ll be able to join?

A couple quick clarifications before the call so we can prep data: 
1) The 200 concurrent figure is an average steady-state for each region (we have separate clusters per region). The 500 bursts are global across regions (we want to see how Redwood handles cross-region fallback).
2) Median request size: for the search prompt body (not including retrieved context) it’s ~40–60 tokens, but when we include the top-5 snippets the median grows to 110–140 tokens — we included a sample trace in the CSV.
3) For the pilot, we need a proposal that avoids cross-tenant cache poisoning — we will require tenant isolation in KV caching or per-tenant cache namespaces. If per-tenant pools are necessary, please call that out in the sizing.

Finally, two asks for the call: please bring an example throughput/latency matrix for both quantized (4-bit) and fp16 variants, and a quick checklist of the telemetry bits we’ll need to expose (trace/span ids, per-request token cost, and model versioning headers).

Thanks — Wed 25/14:00 PT is confirmed from our side.

Best,
Emily Chen
Head of Search
CloudWave Systems
echen@cloudwave.io

----

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <echen@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jake Torres <jake.torres@cloudwave.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sync request — throughput & latency sizing for CloudWave search

Perfect — locking Wed 25 Feb 14:00–14:45 PT (invite to follow). Marcus will lead the deep dive and will bring: 
- A throughput/latency sketch for fp16 and 4-bit quantized variants based on the sample traces you provided. Expect a preliminary table showing tokens/sec per GPU and estimated p95 under conservative batching.
- A recommendation on per-tenant cache namespaces vs. isolated pools and the tradeoffs (cost, latency, operational complexity).
- A short checklist of telemetry (we’ll include span ids, model-version headers, token accounting, and tracing hooks).

Action items for CloudWave before the call (quick wins):
- Paste representative request counts by hour and region into the attached CSV (if you haven’t already).
- Confirm whether the pilot must run inside your us-west-2 VPC or if a hosted dedicated hybrid is OK.

I’ll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link and attach the intake PDF and an internal pre-read. If you want a short 15-min pre-call with Marcus to review the CSV before Wed, we can do Tue 24 at 15:00 PT — say the word.

Thanks — see you Wed.

—Aditya
